narrative: Material PL1__M2DEC9DF exhibits intermittent demand with mean=230.70 units/day and CV=1.01. Demand occurs on 62.8% of working days with notable lumpiness; 2 outliers were winsorised. Lead times average 4.04 days with moderate variability (CV=0.30). The (r,Q) continuous-review model is recommended, with safety stock of 895 units (z=1.645) to achieve 95% service level. Order quantity is capped at 1,345 due to the binding 2,241-unit storage constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) continuous-review model suits PL1__M2DEC9DF because demand, while intermittent, occurs frequently enough (62.8% of days) to justify continuous monitoring rather than periodic review. It minimises total inventory cost by balancing ordering frequency against holding costs, and it naturally accommodates the reorder-point calculation needed to cover lead-time demand variability at the 95% service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity constraint is binding: the recommended policy occupies 100% of available storage (895 SS + 1345 OQ = 2240 units vs. 2240.96 capacity). Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g., using the robust estimate of 1190) would breach the storage limit. Management should consider a capacity expansion to unlock the full EOQ benefit and reduce total annual cost.
